cards.text: Friend, Babylon has carried Judah off into exile (2 Kings 25:21). But Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon left some people behind in the land of Judah, and somebody has to be over them. He picks Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan.

cards.question: The army commanders of Judah hear the news: the king of Babylon has appointed Gedaliah as ___.

cards.text: So the commanders and their men come to see Gedaliah at Mizpah, and four of those commanders get named. I bet that first meeting was TENSE. New boss, and the other side picked him.

cards.question: Which of these men is one of the commanders who come to Gedaliah at Mizpah?

cards.text: Picture it. Judah just fell to Babylon, and now these army men are face to face with Babylon's governor, so Gedaliah takes an oath in front of them and their men.

cards.question: In his oath, what does Gedaliah tell the commanders not to be afraid of?
Gedaliah's advice to the commanders: live in the land and serve the king of ___, and it will be well with you.

cards.text: Sounds like things might finally calm down. Then in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, a member of the royal family, shows up with ten men.

cards.question: Ishmael and his ten men come to Gedaliah at Mizpah. What does Ishmael do?
Ishmael kills Gedaliah but spares everyone who was with him at Mizpah.

cards.text: Babylon's governor is gone. Then all the people, small and great, get up and run, and the army commanders go right along with them.

cards.question: The people and the army commanders flee to Egypt.
Why do the people and the army commanders flee to Egypt?

answers.text: They are afraid of the Chaldeans
They are following the king of Egypt
They are running from a famine

cards.text: Now we go to Babylon, where Jehoiachin, the king of Judah carried off there years before (2 Kings 24:15), is in the thirty-seventh year of his exile. THIRTY-SEVEN YEARS, friend, and I get antsy when the oven timer has two minutes left.

cards.question: In the year Evil-merodach becomes king of Babylon, what does he do for Jehoiachin?

answers.text: He sends him back to Judah

cards.text: And it keeps getting better. Evil-merodach speaks kindly to Jehoiachin, and there are other kings with Jehoiachin in Babylon too.

cards.question: Evil-merodach sets Jehoiachin's throne below the thrones of the other kings with him in Babylon.

cards.text: So Jehoiachin changes out of his prison clothes. When I got out of the junk drawer, I left a whole coat of dust behind, and friend, I did NOT go back for it.

cards.question: Jehoiachin eats at the king's table just once, as a one-time honor.
On top of a seat at his table, the king gives Jehoiachin a daily ___ for the rest of his life.

findings.problem: "So Gedaliah takes an oath" makes the commanders being face to face with Babylon's governor the reason for the oath. 2 Kings 25:24 says only "And Gedaliah took an oath before them," with no reason given. "Judah just fell" also adds a sense of timing that the text doesn't give. Most of the card repeats card 3's setup, and only the oath moves the passage along.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question calls Gedaliah's words "advice." The text calls them an oath that assures them: "Gedaliah took an oath before them and their men, assuring them" (2 Kings 25:24). Card 6 even calls it "his oath."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "The army commanders of Judah" says whose armies these are. The text says only "all the commanders of the armies and their men" (2 Kings 25:23).

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The only humor here is "New boss, and the other side picked him." It reads like a pleasant observation, not a real laugh. Apart from this card, only cards 14 and 18 try a joke. Moments that could hold a laugh, like the reversal in card 16 or the change of clothes, are told flat or only lightly.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "warning" and "guard" aren't the same kind of thing as "portion." After "On top of a seat at his table," which sets up a gift, "warning" reads as an obvious throwaway, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: No earlier card says Jehoiachin is in prison. Card 14 says only that he is in exile, so "He sends him back to Judah" is the natural reasoned pick, and the right answer, release from prison, can only be guessed.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.
